claims.title: Different-channel two-view fiber: a (k^2-k)-parameter signed family (known), with the nonnegative product gauge forced to a common permutation
claims.scope: T = K1^T D_pi K2 with K1, K2 row-stochastic of full row rank k and pi > 0
assumptions: views are conditionally independent given one persistent latent state
the number of latent states k is fixed
exact population laws
nonclaims: the signed parametrization and its J(J-1) dimension are known (Henry-Kitamura-Salanie 2014, Sec. 4.2; Hall-Zhou 2003 for k = 2); only the product-gauge rigidity (b), which supplies the different-channel case set aside by the P1-T7 nonclaims, is claimed here
the dimension count is of the signed parameter set; positivity constraints are only shown to leave a full-dimensional neighbourhood when K1, K2 > 0

claims.title: Binary latent, two views: the sharp identified set of the prior weight is [1 - q_{y*}^2/T_{y*y*}, q_{x*}^2/T_{x*x*}], piecewise rational in the observable law
claims.scope: k = 2 under the hypotheses of ST-T297; {x*, y*} is the observable outcome pair that maximizes the angle between columns of any rank-2 factor of T, equivalently minimizes T_xy^2/(T_xx T_yy); outcomes with q_x = 0 are dropped; the weight is that of the latent favoured by x*
assumptions: k latent states with pi > 0, finite outcome alphabet, row-stochastic K of full row rank k, and k fixed and known

nonclaims: Theorem B specializes the sharp two-component bounds of Henry-Kitamura-Salanie 2014 (Theorem 1) to a shared channel, and the feasible-band mechanism is Lawton-Sylvestre 1971; only the explicit closed form is offered, with no priority claimed
without a label convention the identified set is [L,U] union [1-U,1-L]
the endpoints are rational only once the extreme pair is fixed; they can jump where an outcome probability tends to 0

claims.title: (standard) Within a two-view fiber every Bayes factor equals one and the posterior conditional on T equals the prior conditional on T
